Subject: Offer signing key provisioning and verification for NimbleCloud listing

Hi team,

We are finalizing the NimbleCloud (publisher tenant: nimblecloud-pub) offer and need to complete the publisher key provisioning and signature verification step before we can submit the offer package. Two quick asks:

1) Can you confirm the exact key formats supported by the portal for the offer signing certificate (PEM vs PFX), and whether a hardware-backed key (HSM) with an AAGUID is acceptable for the signing step?
2) What is the verification flow once we upload the key? Is there an automated check in the portal, or does Microsoft perform a manual signature verification/identity proof?

I've attached the Azure offer signing requirements we typically use and a screenshot of the publisher identity page for nimblecloud-pub.

Attachments: azure-offer-signing-requirements.pdf (doc stub), publisher-identity-screenshot.png (image stub)

Goal: unblock the publish window this week.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Partner Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Azure Marketplace Support <azure-marketplace-support@microsoft.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-05T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Offer signing key provisioning and verification for NimbleCloud listing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the details — appreciate the attachments. Short answers below and a short checklist to progress the signing step.

1) Supported formats: The Marketplace portal accepts both PEM and PFX for offer signing. If you upload a PFX, please include the password in the secure field in the portal (do not email it). For HSM-backed keys, we support keys provisioned via Azure Key Vault with a managed HSM (recommended). The portal can perform a key binding to Key Vault if you provide the SPN and role assignment.

2) Verification flow: After key upload/binding, there is an automated signature validation step (portal checks certificate chain, expiration, and key usage). For HSM/KeyVault bindings we also run an async proof-of-possession check (you may receive a verification email to the publisher admin). Manual intervention is only required if the automated checks fail.

Checklist to finish this week:
- Upload PEM or PFX to the publisher tenant
- If using Key Vault/HSM, provide SPN/docs to bind the vault (portal supports ARM template binding)
- Confirm publisher admin email for the PoP verification: liz.nimblecloud@example.com
- Ensure certificate CN matches the registered publisher name

Portal link for key upload: https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Marketplace/PublisherKeyUpload

If you want, we can set up a 30-minute screen share tomorrow to walk the team through the binding step.

Regards,
Azure Marketplace Team
Microsoft Corp.

Thanks for the quick clarification — very helpful. A couple of operational notes from our side:

- NimbleCloud confirmed they will use an Azure Key Vault with MS-managed HSM. They asked whether Redwood can perform the SPN creation and role assignment or if that must be done by their tenant admin.
- I recommend we propose the following minimal set of permissions for the SPN: Key Vault CryptoUser + Reader on the vault resource. If Microsoft needs any specific roles beyond these for binding, please flag.

Action items:
- Karthik: please draft the ARM snippet or guidance for SPN + role assignment that Nimble can run (we can include it in the publisher onboarding doc).
- Kimberly: can you verify our internal runbook covers PoP verification email handling?

Marissa

On Thu, 2026-08-05 at 13:40, Marissa Cole wrote:
> Thanks for the quick clarification — very helpful. A couple of operational notes from our side:
>
> - NimbleCloud confirmed they will use an Azure Key Vault with MS-managed HSM. They asked whether Redwood can perform the SPN creation and role assignment or if that must be done by their tenant admin.

We should avoid creating tenant-scoped principals in customer tenants unless explicitly asked. I suggest we provide a concise ARM template + step-by-step CLI for the nimble tenant admin to run; it’s safer and reduces audit friction. I'll draft the ARM snippet and a short CLI guide today and attach it to the onboarding doc.

Quick checklist for the template:
- Create SPN (az ad sp create-for-rbac)
- Assign Key Vault access policy: set permissions to sign, verify, get
- Assign Resource Reader role on the vault resource

I will also prepare a short test plan for the PoP verification step (including which logs to capture in Key Vault and Azure AD).

Connor
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
